_comment: #460 crypt-Lich canonical. Stands mid-dig ON ruin_surface (the only way onto that map is `ruin_door`'s horns_dig_started gate, so the counter is banked), one cell WEST of `bone_pile_ruin` and facing it -- the wave_b_animate_start posture, reused deliberately rather than invented: the script's first act is to RAISE the player's own skeleton off that pile, so the fight that follows puts `skeleton_ally` and the Lich's `bone_thrall`s on ONE BOARD. That co-presence is the art constraint this feature carries (tint-is-not-disambiguation), and this fixture is what makes it observable instead of argued. BUILD is the Act IV band (`balance-bands-and-policy.md`: 12-14 combined) -- warrior 7 / mage 6 with the band's own loadout, the same allocation `sim_spine_viability.gd`'s `band_act4` measures the encounter at, so the canonical and the balance row are reading one build. [Animate Dead] rides `player_skills` as a fixture affordance (the wave_b precedent); its real Necromancer L5 grant is pinned in test_progression. The counters carry the level ladder honestly (melee_hit 32 for warrior 7, spell_cast 18 for mage 6) -- `test_fixture_coherence` refuses a fixture that holds a level its own accomplishments never earned, and it is right to: a save that could not exist measures nothing.
